assertions.name: cross_anchor_prune_FAILS_and_the_reason_is_sensitivity
assertions.source: c agrees across the two pins to ~1e-7 relative, and that is NOT evidence of anchor-independence -- the test has no power here. c_3 is amplified 2.05889e+6x (extracted through 1/u^3); c is amplified 9.57631x (no magnifier). Ratio 214998.0x. Recorded as a FAILED prune. The c_3 swing reproduces AGENTS.md's recorded 2.3912 % (2.39121 %), which is the calibration.

assertions.name: doubling_identity_is_exact_for_a_genuine_constant_residue_character
assertions.source: chi(q^2) - (2 chi(q)^2 - 1) is at most 1.867e-60 over c in {0.5, 5.968, 11.168, -3.2} -- zero to the arithmetic's floor, for every c. Proved in general by QOU.QBeta.CharacterDoubling.char_doubling_of_constant_residue (sorry-free), which is the hyperbolic analogue of ln(q^2) = 2 ln q.

assertions.name: requirement_function_fails_the_doubling_identity_at_every_point
assertions.source: kappa(q) = Q_codata/(Q_base(q)(1-u^2)) on the z_D base misses chi(q^2) = 2 chi(q)^2 - 1 by at least 59.304 % across q in {q0, 1.5, 2, 3} -- so it is the character of NO constant-residue holonomy, for any c at once (QOU.QBeta.CharacterDoubling.not_constant_residue_character_of_doubling_fails).

assertions.name: no_rescaling_rescues_it_so_the_prune_is_not_a_normalisation_artifact
assertions.source: The doubling identity is NOT scale-invariant and kappa carries the experimental Q_codata as an overall scale, so a single lambda might have rescued it. Solving 2 lam^2 kappa(q)^2 - lam kappa(q^2) - 1 = 0 gives lam(q) spreading 28.8608 % over five points, against |lam - 1| <= 1.556e-61 for a genuine character. One constant cannot do it.

assertions.name: at_a_point_the_exclusion_does_NOT_hold_and_that_is_the_scope
assertions.source: At q0 alone the free c reaches the requirement exactly: c = 5.96831620270888 gives cosh(c ln q0) = kappa to 0.0. So scope-(b) covers 'as a FUNCTION of q' ONLY; a pointwise match is always available and carries no information. Quoting this exclusion without that scope would be the over-claim AGENTS.md's (a)/(b) rule exists to prevent.

assertions.name: the_near_integer_is_recorded_as_a_check_against_and_not_pursued
assertions.source: c at the live cell is 5.96831620271, which is 0.5281 % from 6. Recorded as a check-AGAINST and NOT pursued: a near-integer found by solving against the target is selection against the target (NO FITTING), and the cell is provisional besides -- the 2026-09-13 owner ruling records that its element nuc11_interleaved FAILS the confinement SDP on (2,1) and (1,1,1), so c moves when the element is replaced. No search was run for a reason c should be 6.

assertions.name: the_q_dependent_residue_survivor_is_VACUOUS_not_open
assertions.source: cosh is onto [1, inf), so wherever 1 <= kappa a q-dependent residue reproducing it exists BY CONSTRUCTION -- one sets a(q) := arcosh(kappa(q)), reading the residue off the answer. Measured, kappa on the z_D base stays >= 1 throughout q in (1, 10] (min 1.53328285794 at the low end, rising to 8.02430932715 at q = 10), so the vacuity is not conditional in the physical domain. Proved in general by QOU.QBeta.CharacterDoubling.exists_q_dependent_residue_of_one_le. Same disposition EigenphaseCarrierVacuity gives the elliptic trichotomy's middle branch ('M arbitrary -- CIRCULAR'), reached independently on the hyperbolic side. Only a residue whose q-dependence is DERIVED can carry content.

description: The hyperbolic branch that the ruled base re-opens for route 5 is itself closed for CONSTANT residues. Kohno-Drinfeld fixes hbar = 2 ln q, so a constant-residue generator eigenvalue is c*ln q and its character is cosh(c ln q), which satisfies chi(q^2) = 2 chi(q)^2 - 1 for EVERY c (the cosh double-angle law; the hyperbolic analogue of the ln(q^2) = 2 ln q identity that PhaseFailsLogFunctionalEquation uses to exclude the same holonomy on the elliptic reading). The requirement function kappa(q) = Q_codata/(Q_base(q)(1-u^2)) on the z_D base misses that identity by 59-70 % across q in {q0, 1.5, 2, 3}, and no rescaling rescues it (lambda(q) spreads 28.86 % against lambda == 1 for a genuine character). ALSO REPORTS A FAILED PRUNE: cross-anchor rigidity, the obvious test, has no power here -- c is amplified ~9.6x across the two pins while c_3 is amplified ~2.06e6x through its 1/u^3 extraction, a ratio of 2.15e5, so the pins' agreement on c is evidence about the test and not about c. SCOPE: (b) for 'as a FUNCTION of q' only; at a single q0 the free c reaches any kappa >= 1 and the exclusion does NOT hold. What survives is what the elliptic sibling leaves open -- a q-dependent residue, a non-flat construction, or a q-dependent-parameter transcendental object.

An agent reading only the agreement would conclude c is anchor-independent, which this does NOT show.

scope: (b) for the constant-residue exclusion AS A FUNCTION, citing a proved identity; (a) for every number; explicitly NOT an exclusion at a point. Derives no alpha, selects no base, wires nothing.
